assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators opened a new class of materials defined by topology rather than symmetry breaking. The idea (Kane-Mele), the concrete material proposal and the first transport observation in HgTe quantum wells (Molenkamp and collaborators) form a clean theory-to-experiment chain. As an experimentalist I value that a specific measured edge-channel conductance confirmed the prediction.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step; Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realization. Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposed the HgTe route but are not in the credited names, so the three-person configuration is defensible yet leaves a visible credit question. Other topological-matter pioneers have partly been recognized already.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation in many materials and strong stability of the interpretation; recognition is timely and arguably overdue, with the 2016 prize covering a different part of topology.
uncertainties: Whether the BHZ proposal and Zhang's role would be seen as indispensable to the HgTe observation.
Overlap with the earlier 2016 prize may be argued as reducing novelty.
Facts on exact first-observation priority are from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correction of spherical aberration made sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy routine in transmission electron microscopes, an enabling invention that changed atomic-scale materials physics. It clearly fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion, and its impact on interfaces, oxides and nanostructures is large and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theory of the corrector, Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the first working corrected instrument (with Rose and collaborators). The three-person configuration is natural and well documented in the instrument literature. Earlier electron-microscopy prizes (Ruska) and the Kavli recognition do not complicate the credit.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated in the late 1990s and now used in thousands of instruments worldwide, with very strong independent confirmation; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: I work in this field, so I weigh it with care for bias; a conflict check on Chalmers and microscopy colleagues is warranted.
Contributions of other groups (Krivanek, Zach and others) in related corrector designs could be argued as comparable.
Some committee members might regard this as an instrument advance closer to chemistry or applied physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combined the magic-wavelength idea with ultracold strontium to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, enabling tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, original and highly consequential invention.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group made decisive demonstrations of record accuracy and many-body clock physics. Two laureates give a tidy allocation, though ion-clock and frequency-comb pioneers have been credited in earlier prizes (2005, 2012).
assessment.maturity: Mature, with multiple independent labs reproducing performance and an international roadmap toward redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Others, such as Ludlow and Lemonde, contributed to the clock realization and are not in the credited names.
Overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes in metrology may be seen as an incremental step by some.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-angle prediction of flat bands and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states created the field of twistronics and a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. The discovery is original and has had a large and rapid impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental observations (with Cao and colleagues). The three names support a fair split between theory and experiment, although the experimental first author's role may be debated.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups in several moire materials, but the interpretation of the superconducting pairing and correlated phases is still evolving, so the field is a few years short of settled.
uncertainties: Premature if the committee wants stable understanding of the superconducting mechanism.
Role of Yuan Cao and others in the experimental breakthrough is outside the credited names.
Competition with the 2010 graphene prize may be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and entanglement-based key distribution created a physically secured communication concept that links foundations and technology and now underpins a wide experimental field. The idea is original, simple and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard proposed BB84; Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is a separate, independent conception. The three-name configuration is natural and widely cited. The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments recognized adjacent but different work.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of experiments, satellite and fibre demonstrations and commercial systems, though practical security under device imperfections is still an active area.
uncertainties: The ballot has a near-duplicate candidate; I treat the entry as the key-distribution concept itself.
Whether a prize for a protocol fits 'physics' for some members is a matter of judgement.
Priority claims related to earlier ideas (Wiesner conjugate coding) are from memory and not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC completed the Standard Model's scalar sector and relied on extraordinary detector and analysis achievements. The significance is beyond dispute, even though the 2013 prize honored the theory.
assessment.attribution: A three-person limit is difficult for two collaborations with thousands of members. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding proponents and conceivers of the experiments; Gianotti led ATLAS at the discovery. I choose three founding figures, acknowledging that this allocation is contested and the credited names exclude others.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed by two experiments and later precision measurements; recognition is timely but the awarding question is about configuration rather than science.
uncertainties: Attribution inside large collaborations is unresolved and may be the main obstacle.
The choice between spokespeople at the discovery and founding proponents is a judgment call.
Whether the Higgs experimental discovery is regarded as already covered by 2013 is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics provides strong, controllable light-matter coupling on a chip and is the basis of leading superconducting quantum processors and quantum-limited readout. It is original and has broad technological and scientific consequences.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf are the standard authors of the 2004 proposal and demonstration; the credited names support a theory-plus-two-experiments configuration. Credit may be split from related circuit-QED work such as Devoret's, partly recognized in 2025.
assessment.maturity: Mature with extensive independent confirmation, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits touches adjacent ground and may influence timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may weigh against a near-term second circuit award.
Whether Girvin and Devoret are indispensable is not resolved by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the later identification of a source with IceCube opened a new window onto the cosmos with a one-cubic-kilometre detector in ice. This is a decisive discovery with a major instrument achievement.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube and Karle was a leading figure in the construction and the collaboration's analyses; the two-name configuration is plausible but a large collaboration obscures individual credit. Neutrino astronomy was honored in 2002.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature given statistical evidence of the diffuse flux and source associations such as TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, though source populations remain unclear.
uncertainties: Collaboration credit and the roles of others (for example, Ahrens, Kowalski) are not captured.
Source identification is still based on modest significance in places.
